Article Title: 'Pellet guns can be used in exceptional situations': SC seeks RAF ammunition log from Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text:
SC directs Centre to preserve the ammunition log of the Rapid Action Force.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday observed that police are "empowered to use pellet guns in exceptional situations" while directing the Centre to preserve the ammunition log of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) deployed at Jantar Mantar.The court's observation comes at a time when allegations of pellet gun use against NEET protesters during the CJP-led student protest on July 20 have escalated into a political potboiler in Parliament.A Bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also directed the Delhi government to provide adequate treatment to those protesters who were injured by alleged firing of pellet guns.The bench also observed that when in extreme violent situations police are permitted to use bullets if violence does not get controlled by lathicharge and tear gas, how can they be barred from using pellet guns if a protest, which has turned violent after being hijacked by miscreants for ulterior purposes. The court said all injured persons during protests should be given proper treatment.The top court, however, questioned petitioner and ex-IPS offier Yashovardhan Azad for seeking ban on use of pellet guns against protesters.Meanwhile, a CRPF post-event analysis has said that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters, which included the authorised use of "non-lethal" means like pellet gun.CRPF sources told TOI that upon carefully examining the response of its anti-riot unit, Rapid Action Force, it is evident that force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to effectively control the mob.Around 3-5 protesters were injured by the metal pellets. Also, 47 RAF personnel were injured, with six sustaining head injuries.Moreover, CRPF director general G P Singh came forward to support all his troops taking decisions and actions in bona fide discharge of their duties.Addressing personnel at CRPF investiture ceremony coinciding with its Raising Day Monday, Singh said, "As DG of CRPF, I want to assure each one of you that whether it is an operational battalion or law-and-order unit, whatever decisions you carry out in the bona fide discharge of your duties and which are aligned with interests of the public, the force and the nation, I shall take responsibility for all those decisions and actions. Continue to perform your duties fearlessly. Wherever responsibility or accountability needs to be taken, I will take as the director general".
Article Summary: SC directs Centre to preserve the ammunition log of the Rapid Action Force. Allegations of pellet gun use against NEET protesters have escalated into a political potboiler. CRPF post-event analysis has said that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed.

Article Title: 'Students deserve justice': Rahul Gandhi shares video claiming police brutality during NEET protest
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi seeks SC-monitored probe into police action on students

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Thursday demanded an independent Supreme Court-monitored high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police excesses against students protesting the perpetual paper leaks on July 20."Students deserve justice. An independent SC monitored high powered committee must be constituted to probe brutalities against our students," Rahul said in a post on X while sharing a video claiming police brutality during the protest.The remarks came after Rahul had earlier accused Union Home Minister Amit Shah of being responsible for the police's alleged excesses against protesters, including the reported firing incident.Rahul demanded the removal of Union home minister Amit Shah and called for a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into the alleged use of "lethal force" against student protesters, escalating the Opposition's attack on the government over the police crackdown.Addressing the Lok Sabha, Rahul alleged that Shah either directly authorised the use of pellet guns, shock batons, lathicharge and tear gas against students, making him "culpable of brutalisation" of young protesters, or was unaware of the police action, which, he said, made him "incompetent.""In either case, he has to go," Rahul said, urging Prime Minister Narendra Modi to remove the senior minister from the Cabinet.The allegations triggered strong protests from the treasury benches, with Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju demanding that Gandhi either substantiate his claims with evidence or apologise.Rahul Gandhi also blamed RSS for what he described as the problems afflicting the education sector.The government strongly objected to his remarks, with treasury bench members demanding that he either substantiate his allegations or apologise. They said Rahul Gandhi should not be allowed to continue his speech unless he provided evidence or expressed regret for the claims."You cannot level a charge to grab a headline and get away with it without providing proof," Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said.Union minister Jitendra Singh also said that orders for police firing are issued by a magistrate. Defending the Delhi Police, he said the force had exercised "utmost restraint" while handling the protesters' march on July 20, marking the first such defence by a senior government functionary.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi demands an independent Supreme Court-monitored high-powered committee to investigate alleged police excesses. Rahul had earlier accused Union Home Minister Amit Shah of being responsible for the police's alleged excesses against protesters, including the reported firing incident.

Article Title: 'Even Mughals called Shivaji a chuha': Uddhav likens Gen Z to Maratha warrior
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj

Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Wednesday likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj , saying that even Mughals had called the Maratha warrior a "chuha" (rat), just as the current generation is being called "cockroaches".Addressing a gathering during a book launch in Mumbai, Thackeray said those who had been dismissed as "cockroaches" belonged to Generation Z, roughly between the ages of 13 and 28 and drew a parallel how Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was only 17 when he captured Torna Fort, while Sant Dnyaneshwar was also very young when he wrote the Dnyaneshwari."Those who were insulted as 'cockroaches' belong to what we now call Generation Z roughly from the ages of thirteen or fourteen to twenty-seven or twenty-eight. Wasn't Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj just about that age when he captured Torna Fort at seventeen? Even Shivaji Maharaj was called a 'Chuha' by Mughal. Wasn't Sant Dnyaneshwar also very young when he wrote the Dnyaneshwari? Both faced tremendous opposition in their own time," Thackeray said.He said Shivaji Maharaj had challenged the Mughal Empire despite his young age, arguing that today's youth should not be belittled for speaking out.This comes at a time when political leaders across party lines have increasingly adopted Gen Z terminology to sharpen their political messaging during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.From treasury bench members defending the Centre's reforms to opposition MPs criticising the government's handling of the NEET controversy, lawmakers turned to internet slang more commonly associated with social media than parliamentary debate.BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj invoked Gen Z slang while backing the proposed legislation, using the phrase "clock it", a popular internet expression used to acknowledge or recognise something.Speaking in support of the Bill, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution."On the other hand, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra invoked Gen Z terminology while criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public outreach, arguing that young people were able to see through political messaging."If you want to win over the Gen Z, then making videos with different camera angles will not help. The prime minister needs to change the angle of his heart, not the angle of cameras," Priyanka said."Injustice has been done with youths under your government, accept the truth. Prime Minister Narendra Modi must take responsibility," she added.
Article Summary: Uddhav Thackeray likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. He said that even Mughals had called the Maratha warrior a "chuha" (rat) This comes at a time when political leaders across party lines have increasingly adopted Gen Z terminology.

NEW DELHI: As personnel of Rapid Action Force (RAF), a unit of CRPF , face questions for having fired pellet guns at anti-NEET paper leak protesters, CRPF director general G P Singh has come forward to support all his troops taking decisions and actions in bona fide discharge of their duties.Addressing personnel at CRPF investiture ceremony coinciding with its Raising Day Monday, Singh said, "As DG of CRPF, I want to assure each one of you that whether it is an operational battalion or law-and-order unit, whatever decisions you carry out in the bona fide discharge of your duties and which are aligned with interests of the public, the force and the nation, I shall take responsibility for all those decisions and actions. Continue to perform your duties fearlessly. Wherever responsibility or accountability needs to be taken, I will take as the director general".As TOI reported on Wednesday, a CRPF post-event assessment has found that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and laid down protocols were followed by RAF personnel during the police action against anti-NEET protesters on July 20.In view of this, a source told TOI, no case may be made out against the RAF personnel for causing injuries to 3-5 protesters by firing the metal pellets."Even if a case is registered against the RAF personnel under Section 117 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (voluntarily causing hurt), Section 218 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita will kick in, mandating grant of prosecution sanction with approval to the CRPF DG. At this point, the DG can justify the use of authorised force by RAF personnel, to deny prosecution sanction," said an officer.CRPF probe into July 20 police action, as per sources, has concluded that the force gradient was followed, with pellet guns being used after lower-grade measures like crowd dispersal warnings, tear gas and lathicharge failed to control the unruly elements in the mob.As required by SOP, Delhi police DCP/ACP had, using his delegated authority as executive magistrate, authorised RAF in a signed format, to use civilian force, including firing pellet guns.
Article Summary: CRPF director general G P Singh has come forward to support all his troops taking decisions and actions in bona fide discharge of their duties. A CRPF post-event assessment has found that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and laid down protocols were followed.

Article Title: Rs 28.5 crore cash, Rs 21.5 crore gold: Police raid retired bus driver's house in West Bengal
Article Text:
Five cash-counting machines and several gold-weighing scales were used to assess the worth of the haul.





SURI: Birbhum police on Wednesday raided the house of a retired govt bus driver in Deucha village and seized gold bars and biscuits worth around Rs 21.5 crore, along with two trunkloads of cash. The cash haul had crossed Rs 28.5 crore by late evening, with bundles of notes still being counted.Officers said Minar Mondal, owner of the two-storey house and a relative of influential stone trader Tulu Mondal, and his son were being questioned about the source of the seized wealth and whether they had stashed money and gold at any other location.Five cash-counting machines and several gold-weighing scales were used to assess the worth of the haul.The entire area was cordoned off for the search, which began in the early hours. Several high-ranking district police officers, including ASP Nilesh Gaikwad and DSP (law and order) Kunal Mukherjee, supervised the raid.Minar’s kin Tulu Mondal, a prominent stone trader in the district, was a stone revenue collector during the tenure of the Trinamool govt. Sources said that after retiring from his govt job, Minar was assigned a key responsibility by Tulu.“Minar was in charge of collecting revenue from stone-filled trucks at one of the seven toll gates in the quarry belt of Deucha. Investigators are trying to find out whether he had siphoned off a chunk of the money meant for the govt coffers,” a source said.Tulu was considered a close associate of Anubrata Mondal, once a Trinamool strongman in the district. He was accused of operating illegal stone quarries and implicated in a cattle smuggling case.ED had raided his home and office in 2022. Within 48 hours of the raid, the district police arrested him in a murder case. He was released on bail and allegedly went into hiding after the assembly poll results were declared on May 4.Tulu had grabbed eyeballs in Dec 2024 by hosting a lavish reception for his daughter’s wedding. Celebrities from Bollywood and the Bengali entertainment industry attended the reception in an extravagant venue modelled on the iconic Taj Lake Palace in Udaipur.CM Suvendu Adhikari thanked police for Wednesday’s operation.He posted on X, “The work of our law enforcement agencies in taking strict action against the sand mafia is commendable. Birbhum Police conducted a major raid at the hideout of illegal operator Tulu Mondal — alias Mohammad Najibuddin — in the Mohammad Bazar police station area.”He wrote, “Let it be unequivocally clear: no person with a chequered past who has amassed wealth through the exploitation of public resources and hobnobbing with the then ruling political party will be spared.”He commended the director general of police, superintendent of Birbhum police and district police personnel for the success of the operation.Kunal Ghosh, spokesperson for the Trinamool faction loyal to Mamata Banerjee, said that while those responsible for such crimes should not be spared, the govt should also investigate netas who allegedly patronised such activities.“I hear that those responsible for such crimes were closely linked to netas who now brand themselves as ‘good Trinamool’. I will urge the govt to delve deeper and identify those who shielded such criminals and benefited from their illegal earnings,” he said.
Article Summary: The cash haul had crossed Rs 28.5 crore by late evening, with bundles of notes still being counted. The entire area was cordoned off for the search, which began in the early hours. Five cash-counting machines and several gold-weighing scales were used to assess the worth of the haul.

Article Title: 'Not going to let him get away': Rahul Gandhi targets Amit Shah over police action on NEET protesters; BJP says 'prove it or apologise'

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha on Wednesday plunged into bedlam after leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi blamed home minister Amit Shah for police's alleged excesses against protesters, including firing, riling up treasury benches as Union minister Kiren Rijiju demanded that he either furnish proof or apologise.He also blamed Hindutva organisation RSS for all the ills afflicting the education sector.Government challenged him to prove his allegation or apologise and declared that they would not let Rahul continue with his speech if he did not authenticate or regret making the charge. "You cannot level a charge to grab a headline and get away with it without providing proof," said Rijiju.Union minister Jitendra Singh also stressed that police firings are ordered by a magistrate. He also defended Delhi Police in his reply, saying it exercised "utmost restraint" in handling protesters' march on July 20, a first such assertion from a senior govt functionary."It was made sure that any casualty does not happen," Singh said, refuting the allegations of Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi and other opposition MPs that brutal force was used against protesters.Rahul Gandhi demanded Amit Shah be sacked as home minister and a Supreme Court-monitored probe be ordered into use of "lethal force" against young protesters - raising the stakes in the battle of wits with govt over the police crackdown on students.He said Shah either directly ordered use of pellet guns, shock batons, lathicharge and tear gas on students, which makes him "culpable of brutalisation" of youngsters, or he did not know what police was doing, which makes him "incompetent". "In either case, he has to go," he said, advising PM Narendra Modi to sack the senior minister.Rahul alleged students are still being threatened, with face recognition and Bajrang Dal being used to scare them. "These are our children and govt has no business threatening them or beating them. They have not committed any crime. They should not be punished," he said.He said demand for Shah's sacking was not proforma, raising possibility of the confrontation of last week resuming after the opposition joined parliamentary proceedings to discuss the public exam bill for two days. "Shah is responsible and we are not going to let him get away with it," he said.The renewed aggression from Rahul came at a news conference that he addressed after he could not complete his heavily interrupted speech in Lok Sabha following a clash with BJP benches over his remarks about Shah.After brief adjournments over an "unparliamentary" word, BJP blocked him when he directly linked Shah to the police crackdown. While his remarks were expunged, BJP led by Union minister Kiren Rijiju insisted he tell the source of his claim or apologise.As per Rahul, he was told he would have to apologise if he wanted to complete his speech, but he replied he would never apologise to BJP or RSS.With Shah's photograph on the big screen at Congress's headquarters, Rahul said, "Every child beaten by police should know that this is the man who is responsible for what happened. He takes orders from PM, but he is the man who thrashed you and humiliated you." He slammed Shah for not coming to LS, saying it shows he is "guilty".At the same time, Rahul said he is proud of students who protested and "they had the courage that their parents did not have" to stand up to BJP.Rahul riled BJP by claiming a student told him about three categories of people - "students" who accept they don't know everything; those who think they know everything and pretend to be God, and "andh bhakts" who believe the second category is God.He alleged Dharmendra Pradhan, who had to resign as education minister due to students' stir, was a symbol while the real mess in the education system was created by the RSS.
Article Summary: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi blamed home minister Amit Shah for police's alleged excesses against protesters. Government challenged him to prove his allegation or apologise and declared that they would not let Rahul continue with his speech. Union minister Kiren Rijiju demanded that he either furnish proof or apologise.

NEW DELHI: A 27-year-old customer visiting a Union Bank branch in southwest Delhi's Jaffarpur Kalan to update his Aadhaar card was killed Tuesday after the security guard's gun went off accidentally.The deceased, Manish Kumar, a farmer, was a resident of Issapur village. He is survived by his elderly parents and five older sisters. Police have arrested the security guard, Vinod Kumar, 53, an ex-serviceman.Police said the incident took place around 10.30am when Vinod was loading cartridges into his 12-bore double-barrel gun.The firearm allegedly discharged accidentally, and the bullet struck Manish in the backVinod later told police that he reported late for duty Tuesday and by the time he started loading the cartridges, customers and bank employees had already started pouring in.The sound of the gunshot sent customers and the staff into panic. People rushed towards the entrance after hearing the loud bang and found Manish lying in a pool of blood.Police received a PCR call around 11.06 am alerting them about the incident.The caller informed cops that the guard’s firearm had gone off and a man had been shot and was critical. By the time police reached the spot, Manish had already been rushed to RTR Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.According to police, Vinod, a resident of Majri village in Haryana’s Jhajjar district, served in the Army before retiring in 2018 and had been working with a private security agency for the past two years.Investigators said he was posted at the bank as part of his security duties. He has two sons — one is pursuing an MD course while the other is studying MBBS.Police have seized the weapon involved in the incident and sent it for forensic examination. A post-mortem examination of the deceased has been conducted to ascertain the exact cause of death. The report is awaited. Cops are also scanning CCTV footage to ascertain the sequence of events.A case has been registered under BNS Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder).
Article Summary: Manish Kumar, 27, was visiting a Union Bank branch in southwest Delhi's Jaffarpur Kalan to update his Aadhaar card. Police have arrested the security guard, Vinod Kumar, 53, an ex-serviceman. The firearm allegedly discharged accidentally, and the bullet struck Manish in the back.

Article Title: Supreme Court curbs powers of SC panel, says it can’t pass adjudicatory orders
Article Text:
Supreme Court order may hit similar other statutory bodies

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Limiting the power of National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), Supreme Court has held that it is a recommendatory and advisory body and does not have the authority to pass an adjudicatory order.Abench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih said the commission can send its recommendations to a state or Centre in discharge of its functions. However, an order passed by NCSC is not binding in servicerelated matters, it clarified.“The powers entrusted to NCSC are limited in nature. Clearly, NCSC and its other compatriots under articles 338A and 338B are constitutional bodies with a socially beneficent purpose but quite apparently, the legislature has prescribed a role that is recommendatory and advisory, but certainly not adjudicatory. They are not meant to be bodies taking over adjudicatory functions,” the bench said.The court’s order could be applicable to other statutory and constitutional bodies set up for the benefit of different groups of people like women, the minorities and backward classes.Explaining the clause which says that the commission is empowered to “inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Castes”, the bench said, “it is therefore clear that while it has powers to requisition documents and receive evidence, it does not have the power to make an order in furtherance of that evidence.In other words, NCSC can record a factual finding and then ask the govt concerned, either the Centre or the State, to act thereupon.”It rejected NCSC’s plea that the word “safeguards” mentioned in the provision pertains to enforcement. “Such a submission is difficult to accept in view of the explicit language of the Article. It certainly does not confer adjudicatory power; at best recommendatory in nature,” the court said.Thus, the commission cannot take up the role of a court or an adjudicatory tribunal and determine the rights of parties, court added.
Article Summary: National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) is a recommendatory and advisory body and does not have the authority to pass an adjudicatory order. The court’s order could be applicable to other statutory and constitutional bodies set up for the benefit of different groups of people.

SRINAGAR: Political parties in J&K urged Centre and international human rights organisations to intervene after more than 2 dozen people were allegedly killed in firing by Pakistani security forces in PoK over the past 2 days, where unrest has spiralled into deadly clashes.National Conference president Dr Farooq Abdullah urged UN Human Rights Council to send a team to PoK and asked PM Narendra Modi and external affairs minister S Jaishankar to raise the issue with Pakistan . “If PoK is our part, then why is Centre not protesting? The Vaishno Devi yatra also continued, but only on the traditional track via Ardhkuwari.Jammu-Srinagar national highway remained open for traffic.Kishtwar officials said the school closure notice by the district chief education officer followed instructions from the deputy commissioner in the wake of prevailing rough weather and safety concerns over slippery roads and shooting stones. “Schools located within city limits from Malipeth to Cherhar have been exempted from the closure order and will remain open as usual,” the order stated, adding that official work in educational institutions, wherever applicable, should not be affected.In a separate notice, the Doda administration ordered the closure of all govt and private schools in the district on July 29.Both orders clarified that online classes would continue as per the prescribed schedule.IMD predicted light to moderate rain and thundershowers across J&K over the next several days, with the possibility of heavy to torrential rainfall in parts of Jammu division. The department warned that heavy rain could trigger flash floods, landslides and mudslides at vulnerable locations between July 29 and Aug 2.All major pilgrimages in J&K were suspended on July 19 as a precautionary measure. Article Summary: District authorities in J&K’s Doda and Kishtwar ordered the closure of all govt and private schools in view of inclement weather. Meanwhile, the Amarnath pilgrimage continued only on the Baltal route, with a group of 2,051 devotees embarking on the yatra.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi demands Amit Shah's sacking, seeks SC-monitored probe into protest crackdown

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi Wednesday demanded that home minister Amit Shah be sacked from the govt and a Supreme Court monitored probe be ordered into the use of lethal force against young protesters -- raising the stakes in the battle of wits with the Modi govt over the police crackdown on students.Rahul said Shah either directly ordered the use of pellet guns, shock batons, lathicharge and tear gas on students which makes him “culpable” of brutalisation of youngsters, or he did not know what the police was doing which makes him “incompetent”. “In either case, he has to go,” he said, advising PM Narendra Modi to sack the senior minister.He alleged the students are still being threatened, with face recognition and Bajrang Dal being used to scare them. “These are our children and the govt has no business threatening them or beating them. They have not committed any crime. They should not be punished,” he said.The leader of opposition said the demand for Shah’s sacking was not proforma, raising the possibility of the confrontation of last week resuming after the opposition joined the proceedings to discuss the bill on “unfair means” for two days. Said he, “Shah is responsible and we are not going to let him get away with it.”The renewed aggression from Rahul came at a press conference that he addressed after he could not complete his heavily interrupted speech in Lok Sabha following a clash with the BJP benches over his remarks about Shah. After brief adjournments over an “unparliamentary” word, the BJP blocked him when he directly linked Shah to police crackdown. While his remarks were expunged, the BJP benches led by parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju insisted that he tell the source of his claim or apologise.According to Rahul, he was told that he would have to apologise if he wanted to complete his speech, but he replied that he would never apologise to BJP or RSS.With Shah’s photograph on the big screen at the AICC headquarters, Rahul said, “Every child beaten by police should know that this is the man who is responsible for what happened. He takes orders from the prime minister, but he is the man who thrashed you and humiliated you.” He slammed Shah for not coming to the Lok Sabha, which shows that he is “guilty”.At the same time, Rahul said he is proud of students who protested and “they had the courage that their parents did not have” to stand up to the BJP.He said Shah was fully aware of the police action, and he was repeatedly calling minister Jitendra Singh when the latter came to meet him (during dharna outside PM residence).He said the opposition will ensure justice for students one day, as cops responsible for use of pellet guns and batons are identified in videos and photos.In LS, Rahul riled the BJP by narrating that a student told him about three categories of people – “students” who accept they don't know everything; those who think they know everything and pretend to be God, and “andh bhakts” who believe the second category is God.He alleged Dharmendra Pradhan, who had to resign as education minister, was just a symbol while the real mess in the education system was created by RSS. “The man and the organisation that ran the ministry is called the RSS... They (students) have to buy this nonsensical history that RSS fantasises about. Pradhan is the symbol. Your real enemy is the RSS. They are the people who want you to be andh bhakts,” the LOP said.He complained that he is “silenced” every time he tries to speak in Lok Sabha.He called the bill on unfair means as irrelevant because it is about hiking punishment after paper leak when the demand is to reform the system to make it paper leak-proof.He said Modi has lost his image which was a “balloon” that had been inflated with heavy investments.

Article Title: 'Was given a full opportunity': BJP counters Rahul's 'not allowed to speak' claim in Lok Sabha
Article Text:
BJP counters Rahul's 'not allowed to speak' claim in Lok Sabha

Patra defends Rijiju, Rajnath Singh

Rahul alleges police brutality against students

BJP rejects firing allegation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Sambit Patra on Wednesday hit back at Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi over his claim that he was not allowed to speak in the House, saying the Congress leader was given an opportunity to speak and that the objections raised during his speech were related to parliamentary rules.Patra also defended parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju and defence minister Rajnath Singh, rejecting Rahul 's allegation that he was repeatedly interrupted and prevented from completing his speech.The BJP leader's remarks came after Rahul addressed a press conference following a stormy Lok Sabha session, during which the Congress leader alleged that he was denied an opportunity to speak after holding union home minister Amit Shah responsible for alleged police brutality against student protesters during the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march.Reacting to Gandhi's claim, Patra said several opposition MPs, including Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, had been given an opportunity to participate in the debate and questioned why Rahul Gandhi would have been denied the same opportunity."At 6 PM today, Rahul Gandhi once again held a press conference and tried to mislead people by distorting the facts. First, he alleged that he was not allowed to speak. I have said this repeatedly: when 45 Members were given an opportunity to speak, why would Rahul Gandhi not be allowed to speak? When Priyanka Vadra was given an opportunity to speak, and she too made several allegations, why would Rahul Gandhi not be allowed to speak? Rahul Gandhi was given a full opportunity to speak, but he could not do so," Patra said.Congress MP had earlier alleged that he repeatedly asked Speaker Om Birla to restore order in the House so that he could continue speaking."As you saw today, the leader of the opposition was not allowed to speak in the Lok Sabha. Multiple times, I asked the Speaker to bring order to the House so that I could speak. Multiple times, Rajnath Singh ji and others were allowed to speak, but I was not allowed to speak," Gandhi said at his press conference.Gandhi alleged that the reason given to him was his remarks holding Shah responsible for the alleged police action against protesting students. He further claimed that he was told he could continue speaking if he apologised, but said he refused to do so.The Lok Sabha proceedings had witnessed sharp exchanges during the debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. The Bill was eventually passed by the House after a prolonged debate.Patra accused Gandhi of 'shifting the goalposts' after the BJP rejected his allegation that students were shot at during the protest."If there's one person from whom you should learn how to shift the goalposts, it is Rahul Gandhi. I went back and listened to what Rahul Gandhi said in the House today. He said that students were shot at and that the Home Minister had ordered the firing," Patra said.He said BJP leaders, including Jitendra Singh, Piyush Goyal and Rijiju, had already stated that no firing took place and challenged Gandhi to produce evidence."If you have any evidence of bullets being fired, show it. If you have any ballistic report, produce it. So now Rahul Gandhi has shifted the goalposts. This habit of changing the goalposts is an old one for him," Patra said.Patra also questioned Gandhi's claim that he had personally seen Shah speaking continuously with police officers and Jitendra Singh over the phone during the protest."In his press conference today, Rahul Gandhi claimed that he personally saw the Home Minister speaking continuously with police officers over the phone and also speaking with Jitendra Singh. How did he see that? Was he sitting inside the Home Minister's office?" Patra said.Patra also defended the conduct of Rijiju and Rajnath Singh during the proceedings, saying the parliamentary affairs minister's objections were justified under the rules of the House."Rahul Gandhi alleged that Kiren Rijiju and Rajnath Singh interrupted him, while he himself was not given an opportunity to speak. First of all, the two or three objections raised by Kiren Rijiju were entirely justified. Those objections were regarding the use of the unparliamentary word which, under the rules of Parliament, cannot be used on the floor of the House. As the Parliamentary Affairs Minister, it was his responsibility to seek clarification on that," Patra said.He said Rijiju had not acted aggressively and instead asked Gandhi to follow parliamentary rules."Kiren Rijiju's demeanour, body language, and choice of words reflected decency, humility, and composure. He was not angry. In a calm manner, he said, 'We want to hear you. Please do not use the word, because the House functions according to parliamentary rules,'" Patra said.Patra also said Rajnath Singh had appealed to Gandhi to continue his speech and asked members of the Treasury Benches to listen to the Leader of Opposition."Defence Minister Rajnath Singh made only one appeal. He said, 'Rahul ji, please speak,' and appealed to the members of the Treasury Benches to listen to Rahul Gandhi carefully. What greater example of democratic tradition could there be than that?" Patra said.The Parliament row came against the backdrop of a larger political dispute over the alleged police action against students who participated in the July 20 march towards Parliament.Gandhi, in his press conference, repeated his allegations that students were subjected to excessive force and claimed that pellet guns, electric batons and lathis fitted with nails were used during the crackdown."They were shot with pellet guns. One boy who was shot with a pellet gun is most likely to lose his eye and may not be able to see. I have seen the AIIMS medical certificate, which shows that he was shot with pellet guns. Shock batons were used, not just normal lathis, lathis with nails. Where did the police get this idea from?" Gandhi said.He also alleged that Shah was responsible for the alleged police action and demanded his removal."Now there are two possibilities. Either Amit Shah gave the order to shoot people with pellet guns, beat people with lathis with nails, and use electric batons, or he did not know it was happening. If he did not know, he is incompetent. If he ordered it, he is culpable. In either case, he has to go. And every single child who has been beaten must know this," Gandhi said.Rahul also demanded an independent probe into the alleged police action, which is being monitored by the Supreme Court.Patra separately rejected Rahul's allegation that police fired bullets at students during the protest and said the Congress leader was making baseless claims against the Home Minister."Rahul Gandhi said that the students were shot at under the orders of Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Piyush Goyal, Kiren Rijiju and even BJP in its press conference has explicitly cleared that no firing took place. If there are any cartridges, ballistic reports, please show," Patra said.He also questioned Gandhi's claim that Shah had ordered the alleged firing."Rahul Gandhi claimed to have heard the conversation of the Union Home Minister, how is it possible? He earlier lied about Late Manohar Parrikar and Late Sushma Swaraj on Rafael deal. Now he is making such claims," Patra said.The BJP has accused Gandhi of spreading misinformation and attempting to create confusion over the events surrounding the student protests.The party has also demanded that Gandhi apologise for what it described as baseless allegations made inside Parliament.
Article Summary: BJP MP Sambit Patra hits back at Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi over his claim that he was not allowed to speak in the House. Patra also defended parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju and defence minister Rajnath Singh, rejecting Rahul's allegation he was repeatedly interrupted and prevented from completing his speech. Gandhi claimed he was denied an opportunity to speak after holding union home minister Amit Shah responsible for alleged police brutality against student protesters.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Wednesday rejected claims that a woman protester sustained a gunshot injury during the Cockroach Janata Party's July 20 march, saying her medico-legal certificate (MLC) showed only a simple blunt-force injury.In a post on X, Delhi Police said claims circulating on social media were not supported by the protester's medical records.According to the police, the MLC prepared at Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital recorded a lacerated wound in front of the right tragus, with the nature of injury described as blunt."As per the doctor's opinion, it is a simple injury and there is no evidence of gunshot injury. Article Summary: Delhi Police reject claims that a woman protester sustained a gunshot injury during Cockroach Janata Party's July 20 march. They say her medico-legal certificate (MLC) showed only a simple blunt-force injury. The MLC prepared at Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital recorded a lacerated wound.

How can Rahul Gandhi make such false allegations? He should apologise in the House and apologise to the country," he said.Calling Rahul "frustrated", Goyal claimed students had "rejected" the Congress leader."There is no cure for some people. The Leader of the Opposition made such baseless and false statements on the floor of the House. There was no firing, yet such baseless allegations were made inside Parliament. I strongly condemn it," he added.Replying to the debate, Union Minister Jitendra Singh accused Rahul Gandhi of politicising the issue instead of participating in a constructive discussion."This legislation has been brought with great sensitivity and reflects the commitment of Prime Minister Narendra Modi towards ensuring fairness in public examinations. Instead of participating in a constructive discussion or offering suggestions, the Opposition is trying to politicise the issue," Singh said.He also criticised Rahul's conduct in Parliament."I am surprised by the behaviour of the leader of the opposition. And every single child who has been beaten must know this," he added.Reacting to Rahul's remarks, BJP MP Sambit Patra defended the objections raised by treasury bench members during the Congress leader's speech in the Lok Sabha."Rahul Gandhi alleged that Kiren Rijiju and Rajnath Singh interrupted him, while he himself was not given an opportunity to speak. BENGALURU: In May 2026, the Chief Justice of India made an offhand, dismissive remark about unemployed young Indians being like cockroaches. Ten weeks later, a Union minister had resigned, tens of thousands of protesters had marched on Parliament, and a satirical party named after the insult was the biggest story in the country — not necessarily in that order!Nobody involved in that first remark could have predicted where it would end up. That gap, between how small these things start and how large they end up, is the story of Indian student politics itself.It is, in fact, the pattern that connects nearly every major student agitation since independence, laid out in the timeline alongside this piece. A hostel mess-fee hike in Ahmedabad brought down a state govt. A poetry reading on a university lawn became a national argument about sedition.A single self-immolation outside a Delhi college reshaped a decade of caste politics. Indian students, again and again, have turned small, local sparks into fires. Not because the sparks themselves were extraordinary, but because they landed on reservoirs of frustration, economic distress, discrimination, corruption, a sense of being unheard, that were already primed to catch. Few groups in Indian public life have intervened so often, so unpredictably, or with such little warning.India has one of the youngest populations in the world, and its colleges concentrate huge numbers of young people in one place, with time and energy that older, more encumbered protesters often can’t spare — but it isn’t that students have less at stake.It’s that what’s at stake for them is the future itself: the job market they’re about to enter, the country they’re about to inherit, the fairness of the exam or the quota or the citizenship rule that will decide their next decade.Campuses also come with built-in organising infrastructure: hostels, unions, canteens, and, increasingly, group chats that can turn a local grievance into a national one within hours. Students also carry a kind of moral capital unlike any other in Indian public culture: the idea, inherited from the independence movement itself, that young people protesting is a sign of a healthy conscience rather than a threat to order.But structure alone doesn't explain the pattern. India has produced at least 13 agitations substantial enough to, in different ways, influence Indian politics since 1947 — from the 1959 Bengal food riots to the Cockroach Movement. Look closely at five of them across seven decades, and a consistent anatomy emerges: the way these movements start, escalate, provoke the state, and either win, lose, or curdle into something else.In Dec 1973, students at an Ahmedabad engineering college struck over a 20% hike in hostel mess fees. Layered onto soaring food prices and corruption allegations against the state’s chief minister, the strike metastasised within weeks into the Navnirman Andolan. Curfews were imposed in 44 towns; the army was deployed.Facing sustained pressure, chief minister Chimanbhai Patel resigned in Feb 1974, and when the assembly wouldn’t dissolve on its own, veteran leader Morarji Desai’s hunger strike and continued student pressure forced fresh elections anyway. It remains the only instance in independent India’s history of sustained public agitation toppling an elected govt outright — and as per multiple accounts, it directly inspired Jayaprakash Narayan’s (JP) much larger Bihar Movement weeks later, which fed into the political climate that produced both the 1975 Emergency and Congress’ historic 1977 defeat.After electoral rolls turned up apparent non-citizens, the All Assam Students’ Union launched a movement demanding detection and deportation of illegal immigrants. What followed is among the longest continuous student-led agitations in Indian history: blockades, election boycotts, and periods of horrific ethnic violence, including the 1983 Nellie massacre, in a movement whose overall toll has been estimated above 850 deaths.It ended with the 1985 Assam Accord, which set a cutoff date for citizenship claims and promised cultural safeguards still only partially delivered today. AASU leaders converted the movement into a political party, the Asom Gana Parishad, and won the state election that followed.When the govt moved to implement the Mandal Commission’s 27% OBC quota in central jobs, upper-caste students across northern India erupted in protest. On Sept 19, 1990, 19-year-old Delhi University student Rajeev Goswami set himself on fire outside his college; he survived with severe burns but never fully recovered. His act triggered a wave of copycat self-immolation attempts nationwide. The quota was implemented anyway, and VP Singh’s govt fell within months for reasons beyond Mandal alone — proof that a movement can dominate the national imagination for years without reversing the policy that provoked it.Student-led sit-ins against the Citizenship Amendment Act spread from Jamia Millia Islamia to campuses nationwide, but the defining moment came on the night of Dec 15, 2019, when Delhi Police entered Jamia’s campus, including its library, and used batons and tear gas on students inside. That single raid, captured on phone cameras, played an important role in nationalising the anti-CAA movement than months of organizing had. The law remained on the statute books and was later notified, even though the protests fundamentally reshaped the national debate.A dismissive remark about unemployed youth being like “cockroaches” was turned into satire by a strategist who founded the Cockroach Janata Party — a parody of the ruling party’s name, with an AI-generated mascot. Fuelled by anger over leaked entrance exams and graduate unemployment near 40%, it grew from an online joke to hundreds of thousands of members within weeks. On July 20, 2026, roughly 20,000 protesters tried to march on Parliament; police used tear gas and batons, injuring nearly 180 people.Rather than back down, the movement camped at Jantar Mantar and spread to a dozen cities. On July 25, education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned — the core demand met in about ten weeks, a fraction of the time earlier movements took to win anything at all.The five above are the clearest cases, but the other eight matter just as much.s — there had already been other student protests in places like Travancore and Hyderabad — when a famine-level food crisis and police firing on a mass rally pulled students into the streets alongside workers and peasants — establishing, for the first time, that this kind of politics was legitimate in the new republic.Student-led protests against the imposition of Hindi as the sole official language ultimately led the govt to guarantee English would continue indefinitely, and permanently reshaped Tamil Nadu’s politics around the DMK., saw students mobilise around regional neglect and job inequities decades before the state itself was created in 2014 — a reminder that some of these movements take generations to pay off, if they ever do., is where JP’s “Total Revolution” turned a student agitation against corruption and unemployment into a national coalition; when Indira Gandhi responded by declaring the Emergency in 1975, students — opposition parties, socialists, RSS cadres, trade unions also operated from underground — were among groups that kept organised dissent alive underground until elections finally returned in 1977., saw medical and engineering students protest the extension of OBC quotas to central higher-education institutions. The courts upheld most provisions of the policy in 2008, making this the direct sequel to 1990’s argument, fought with less violence but the same underlying tension., wasn’t organised by any student union — it was a largely leaderless, student-heavy public eruption after the gangrape and murder of a young physiotherapy student (Nirbhaya case), and one of the rare cases here that produced fast legislative change: the 2013 criminal law reforms toughening rape sentencing., was smaller in scale but longer in duration: FTII students struck for 139 days over the appointment of a chairman they saw as a political pick, keeping alive the broader argument about political interference in public institutions even though the appointment itself stood., delivered two separate shocks in one year: Dalit scholar Rohith Vemula’s suicide, after his suspension amid political pressure, reopened a national reckoning over caste discrimination on campus. Weeks later, the arrest of JNU Students’ Union president Kanhaiya Kumar on sedition charges, after a campus event, turned “anti-national” speech into one of the decade’s defining and most polarising arguments.Four patterns recur across all thirteen movements above, not just the five examined in depth.As the opening of this piece argued, the size of the spark has never predicted the size of the fire. What decides that is how much pre-existing frustration was already sitting there, waiting for something to ignite it.In case after case, the decisive escalation wasn’t the original grievance but the visible use of force against students: police firing in Calcutta in 1959 and Madurai in 1965, the Jamia library raid in 2019, the tear-gassing at Jantar Mantar in 2026. Violence against students, especially once captured on camera, has repeatedly turned local protests into national ones and made the state's own response the story.Self-immolation recurs across this history, most starkly in 1990, as a form of protest with few real parallels in other democracies’ student movements — a sign both of the intensity of feeling involved and of a media culture in which one person's extreme act can shift public opinion faster than a rally of thousands.Of the 13 movements above, only Navnirman clearly toppled a govt outright. A handful won specific, bounded concessions — the 1965 language guarantee, the 2013 rape-law reforms, Pradhan's 2026 resignation. Several others, including Mandal, the JNU sedition case, and Anti-CAA, ended without the underlying policy being reversed at all, even as they reshaped public debate for years.The honest lesson of seventy years of student politics is that these movements are far better at forcing a national conversation, or costing one official their job, than at reversing a government's core commitments. What has changed is speed, not shape. In 1974 and 1990, it took months or years for a local grievance to become a national reckoning, carried by hostel meetings and cyclostyled pamphlets.In 2026, it took ten weeks, carried by a meme and a mascot. The grammar is identical either way: a grievance, a trigger, a confrontation with the state, and an outcome judged by whether it produced a resignation, a repealed law, or just a memory.
Article Summary: India has produced at least 13 agitations substantial enough to, in different ways, influence Indian politics since 1947. Look closely at five of them across seven decades, and a consistent anatomy emerges: the way these movements start, escalate, provoke the state, and curdle into something else.

Article Title: 'Citizens have every right to demand answers': CJP responds to Delhi Police notice to X over 'derogatory content'
Article Text:
CJP responds to Delhi Police notice to X over 'derogatory content'

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) on Wednesday criticised a Delhi Police notice to social media platform X seeking the removal of allegedly derogatory and defamatory content targeting constitutional authorities, saying citizens have the right to question elected representatives and demand accountability.In a post on X, the CJP said criticism of public officials should not be treated as a criminal act and argued that citizens have a right to raise questions about the functioning of the government."Since when is an elected representative above questioning? In a functioning democracy, citizens have every right to demand answers and accountability from their PM. By treating online criticism as a criminal offense and a threat to "public order", the state machinery is sending a chilling message: the Prime Minister is beyond the reach of public scrutiny," CJP wrote in a post on X.The CJP's remarks came after Delhi Police wrote to social media platform X seeking the removal of content allegedly containing 'derogatory, malicious and defamatory content' targeting constitutional authorities.In its notice, the Delhi Police asked X to 'immediately delete/remove' the alleged post or video and provide complete details of the account that uploaded the content. The information sought includes the user's full name, address, contact number and email ID.The police also sought the account's login and logout details, along with corresponding timestamps and any other information that could assist the investigation.X has also been asked to preserve all data related to the post or video for the ongoing probe and provide a certificate under Section 63(4) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA).The latest notice comes days after Delhi Police directed multiple social media platforms to remove posts and videos containing offensive and abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi that were allegedly uploaded during student protests at Jantar Mantar and the violence linked to the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' march.According to police officials, several posts containing abusive language targeting the Prime Minister surfaced across social media platforms during the protests and subsequent clashes in the national capital.Delhi Police's social media monitoring team has been scanning online platforms for objectionable content linked to the protests. Officials said notices are being issued to social media intermediaries whenever such posts are identified.Police said several posts and videos containing abusive remarks against the Prime Minister have already been removed following such notices.The monitoring exercise is continuing, with cyber and social media teams keeping track of online activity linked to the protests and identifying content that may violate applicable rules.The party's statement comes amid heightened political tensions following the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' march, during which students protesting alleged irregularities in NEET and CBSE examinations clashed with security personnel while marching from Jantar Mantar towards Parliament.The protests also triggered a wider political dispute over alleged police action against students and the registration of cases against protesters.The Supreme Court has separately been hearing pleas concerning alleged police excesses during the protests. The court has stressed the constitutional protection of peaceful protest while also noting that violence and attacks on police personnel cannot be permitted.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party responds to Delhi Police notice to X over 'derogatory content' CJP says criticism of public officials should not be treated as a criminal act. Delhi Police wrote to social media platform X seeking the removal of content.

Article Title: NEET protest: All SOPs followed, pellet gun use on protesters authorised, reveals CRPF review
Article Text:
File photo: July 20 NEET protest march

‘Police, RAF attacked with stones, iron rails’

Poll Vote & Share your view Should police forces utilize non-lethal measures like pellet guns to control protests? Yes, it helps maintain order No, alternative methods should be used Only if extreme violence occurs 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: All standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters, which included the authorised use of "non-lethal" means like pellet gun, a CRPF post-event analysis has said.CRPF sources told TOI that upon carefully examining the response of its anti-riot unit, Rapid Action Force, it is evident that force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to effectively control the mob. Around 3-5 protesters were injured by the metal pellets. Also, 47 RAF personnel were injured, with six sustaining head injuries.When contacted, CRPF DG G P Singh said the matter was "sub judice" and any findings or view of the force on RAF action would be placed before Supreme Court. RAF sources said the use of force on July 20 was authorised by Delhi Police, in line with the SOPs and the law.Sources claimed the mob had some motivated elements attacking personnel of Delhi Police and RAF with stones and, in some cases, even iron rails.As per BNSS, an executive magistrate may order use of civil force to disperse an unlawful assembly after carefully assessing the situation.In Delhi, this magisterial authority is vested with the Delhi Police commissioner, and delegated to junior commissioners till the level of the assistant commissioner of police. “RAF deployed at protest sites uses anti-riot gear only with authorisation; which in this case came from the DCP/ACP in charge of the protest site. Such authorisation is in writing and as per a format used at all sites of unlawful assembly; no order is given verbally,” said an officer.CRPF sources said pump action guns are an approved, “non-lethal” measure to control unlawful assemblies. “Their use, with the force gradient being followed and under authorisation by the competent officer, is as per the SOP,” said an officer.J&K high court had, in its 2016 ruling on a PIL challenging pellet use, said: “So long as there is violence by unruly mobs, use of force is inevitable. What kind of force has to be used at the relevant point of time or in a given situation has to be decided by the persons in charge of the place where the attack is happening. This court in writ jurisdiction, without any finding rendered by the competent forum/authority cannot decide whether the use of force in a particular incident is excessive or not. ”Supreme Court later dismissed the special leave petition against this order, stating, “The use of pellet guns, if at all done by any agency, has not only not been barred, but validated through these orders.”
Article Summary: All standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters. CRPF sources said force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to effectively control the mob.

Article Title: Three firefighters killed as deadly wildfires rage across southern Europe
Article Text:
The wildfires now stretch across a vast area from the Atlantic coast.

Three firefighters died while battling fast-moving wildfires in Greece as an intense heatwave continues to fuel blazes across large parts of southern Europe, forcing hundreds of thousands of people from their homes and stretching emergency services.Greece's fire department said the firefighters lost their lives while tackling separate fires on the island of Crete and in the country's southern mainland. The deaths came as soaring temperatures and strong winds made firefighting operations increasingly difficult.The wildfires now stretch across a vast area from the Atlantic coast to the eastern Mediterranean, affecting countries including France, Spain, Greece and Turkey. Fire experts have expressed concern over the number of large blazes burning close to populated areas, warning that many remain difficult to contain.France recorded temperatures of 38C in Bordeaux on Wednesday, where firefighters prevented a major forest fire from spreading into nearby suburbs. In Spain, temperatures reached 37C in Madrid as authorities reported progress in containing the country's largest wildfire on record.Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said the blaze west of Madrid had been "technically stabilised", although emergency crews continued working to eliminate remaining hotspots.Emergency services said dozens of firefighting teams managed to contain the Madrid-area fire overnight. However, another wildfire near València remained out of control despite relatively cooler temperatures of around 32C.Speaking from the Navalcarnero emergency command centre, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said conditions around Madrid were improving but warned that the coming hours would remain critical."I believe the next 12 hours will be very important," Sánchez said. "They are going to be decisive in consolidating the work done by the national civil protection system."He also noted that the Madrid wildfire had become the first in Spain's history to be raised to "operational level 3", requiring the national government to assume responsibility for managing the emergency.Authorities across western Europe said the latest heatwave, the region's fourth this summer, has significantly increased the risk of wildfires. High temperatures combined with powerful winds have made existing fires harder to extinguish while raising the possibility of previously controlled blazes reigniting.Fresh fires also prompted new evacuations in parts of Greece and Turkey.In France, officials said calm weather overnight had allowed firefighters to quickly deal with flare-ups. However, authorities warned that changing weather conditions could make firefighting more difficult in the coming days.The Gironde prefecture said 126 firefighters had been injured since the wildfire began, although the total area burned remained unchanged at about 42,000 hectares on Wednesday morning.According to data from the European Forest Fire Information System, France has recorded its largest area burned by wildfires, while both France and Spain have experienced an unusually high number of fires for this stage of the year.More than 330,000 people across southern Europe have been forced to leave their homes or hotels because of the fires.As conditions improved in some areas, officials lifted evacuation orders around Bordeaux, Madrid and València, allowing many residents to return. Some found their homes damaged or destroyed, with buildings reduced to burnt shells and personal belongings charred by the flames.The European Union has expanded support for countries battling the fires. Earlier this week, the European Commission deployed seven aircraft and four helicopters to France from several member states, including Sweden and Turkey.Spain also received international assistance, with six firefighting aircraft from Greece, Italy and Turkey, along with 134 personnel and 41 vehicles from Portugal. A Super Puma helicopter from Serbia was expected to arrive in Madrid on Wednesday, followed by another 40 emergency personnel and 18 vehicles.The European Union's crisis management authorities warned that the wildfire season is far from over and said they expect further outbreaks in countries such as Italy and Greece in the coming weeks as extreme summer conditions persist.
Article Summary: Greece's fire department said the firefighters lost their lives while tackling separate fires on the island of Crete and in the country's southern mainland. The deaths came as soaring temperatures and strong winds made firefighting operations increasingly difficult. The wildfires now stretch across a vast area from the Atlantic coast to the eastern Mediterranean.

Article Title: Russia launches overnight ballistic missile attack on Ukraine, killing 13
Article Text:
Photo credit: Reuters

Ukraine expands strikes on Russia's logistics network

Russia launched a wave of overnight air strikes across Ukraine on Thursday, killing at least 13 people, including one in Kyiv. In the attacks that reached as far as the western city of Lviv, prompted neighbouring Poland to scramble fighter jets to secure its airspace.Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko warned about the ballistic missiles heading towards the capital and urged residents to take shelter. Explosions were then heard in Kyiv, according to a Reuters witness. In the western city of Lviv, local officials said two apartment buildings were damaged and six people were injured.The attacks also inflicted heavy casualties elsewhere in the country. Six people, including two children, were killed in the Dnipropetrovsk and Poltava regions, while in Zelenskyy's hometown of Kryvyi Rih, six more people lost their lives after what local officials said was a direct strike by a Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile.Among those killed in Kryvyi Rih were two girls aged 5 and 12. Eight other people were injured in the strike. Oleksandr Vilkul, head of the city's defence council, said the missile was launched from Russia's Voronezh region and hit the home of a large family. Describing it as "a dark night", he warned that the death toll could rise as emergency workers continued clearing the rubble.In the western city of Lviv, near the Polish border, rescue workers searched through the debris after Russian missiles damaged two apartment buildings and injured 15 people, according to local officials.Earlier, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had warned that Russia was likely preparing a massive attack. Following the strikes, he said Ukraine's ability to protect its people depended on its allies willingness to provide more air defence missiles.The appeal came as Zelenskyy returned from the United States, where he said President Donald Trump had agreed to provide Ukraine with licences for Patriot missile systems."It is important that our partners fully understand what is happening and that the protection of people's lives depends directly on their willingness, or lack of willingness, to provide air defence ​missiles," Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram.Poland, a member of the European Union and Nato that shares a border with Ukraine, scrambled fighter jets and activated its air defence network as a precaution following the Russian missile strikes.In a post on X, the Polish armed forces said fighter aircraft and an airborne early warning aircraft had been deployed, while ground-based air defence and radar reconnaissance systems were placed on the highest state of readiness to safeguard the country's airspace. The military said the measures were preventive in nature.Ukraine's long-range drone campaign continued to target Russia's logistics infrastructure, with a warehouse belonging to the country's largest online retailer, Wildberries, catching fire in the western city of Penza.Regional Governor Oleg Melnichenko said one person was injured and around 200 people were evacuated after the attack. The incident came just a day after Wildberries was forced to evacuate another facility in central Russia following a separate Ukrainian drone strike.Following the latest attack, Wildberries said it had rerouted its supply chains to minimise disruptions. The company has increasingly become a target of Ukrainian drone strikes, which have repeatedly hit its warehouse network across Russia.According to the company and local authorities, nearly a dozen Wildberries warehouses have been damaged in recent attacks, destroying about 10% of its storage capacity and causing losses for tens of thousands of small businesses that rely on the platform.The repeated disruptions have also affected ordinary Russians, many of whom depend on online retail as a primary source of income, while Ukraine's campaign against energy facilities, refineries and logistics infrastructure continues to strain Russia's economy.The financial impact is also being felt in the banking sector. Russia's largest lender, Sberbank, has warned that it may need to increase loan-loss provisions as the sustained attacks on Wildberries weigh on the finances of online retailers and their suppliers.
Article Summary: Poland scrambled fighter jets and activated its air defence network as a precaution following the Russian missile strikes. Ukraine's long-range drone campaign continued to target Russia's logistics infrastructure. A warehouse belonging to the country's largest online retailer, Wildberries, caught fire in the western city of Penza.

Article Title: Watch: US launches 'surprise attack' across Iran targeting IRGC facilities
Article Text:
US forces carried out a large-scale wave of strikes against targets in Iran

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) on Thursday said its forces carried out a large-scale wave of strikes against targets in Iran in response to what it described as attempted missile attacks on US forces a day earlier.According to CENTCOM, the operation targeted dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) facilities in a "surprise attack" that included military command centres, missile and drone sites, coastal surveillance and defence installations, and maritime capabilities."CENTCOM assets struck dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets ‌in Iran, including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defense sites, and maritime capabilities," the US Central ⁠Command said in a statement.The strikes came hours after US President Donald Trump vowed to respond "very hard" following Iran's reported missile attack on a military base in Jordan hosting US troops.Also See: Iran War Live Updates Iranian state media reported that two people were injured in strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Explosions were also reported in Khuzestan province in the country's southwest.Elsewhere, drone strikes triggered fires on two natural gas vessels at Egypt's Damietta Port, according to British maritime security firm Ambrey.The vessels included a US-owned floating storage facility and a Greek-owned tanker. The source of the attacks was not immediately known, and no injuries were reported.The fresh attacks on multiple fronts, following several days of relative calm, have heightened fears of a renewed escalation in the conflict. They also highlight the challenges of de-escalating the five-month-long war, which has disrupted global trade and rattled the world economy.Before the latest escalation, mediators had expressed optimism about bringing the United States and Iran back to the negotiating table.However, efforts to revive talks faltered in recent weeks as fighting resumed in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route that has once again been effectively closed due to Iranian attacks.
Article Summary: US Central Command (CENTCOM) on Thursday said its forces carried out a large- scale wave of strikes against targets in Iran. The operation targeted dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) facilities. Strikes came hours after US President Donald Trump vowed to respond "very hard" following Iran's reported missile attack on a military base in Jordan.

Article Title: 'Mulaqat with the bravest, Umar Khalid': Kerala BJP chief cites CJP spokesperson Saurav Das's old post, asks to choose leaders 'wisely'
Article Text:
In a post on X, Chandrasekhar shared Saurav Das's old social media post in which he had described Khalid as the "bravest" and said he had "mad respect" for him.





THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Kerala BJP president Rajeev Chandrasekhar on Wednesday took a swipe at leaders of the recent student protests in Delhi, citing an old social media post by CJP leader Saurav Das praising jailed student activist Umar Khalid.In a post on X, Chandrasekhar shared Das's old social media post in which he had described Khalid as the "bravest" and said he had "mad respect" for him.Khalid was arrested in connection with the 2020 northeast Delhi riots case and remains in jail.Without naming anyone, Chandrasekhar urged students and parents to "choose wisely" and questioned whether they wanted their future shaped by people whose "ideology is dividing and breaking up India.""To the many genuine students and their parents who protested with their genuine grievances — take a look at this pic and its msg. And choose who you are with wisely," he said.The BJP leader asserted that protests turning violent would not be tolerated and said anyone attempting to undermine the country, democracy or its integrity must be opposed."We didn't come so far as a nation (with all our pluses and minuses) to be undermined by this lot.WILL NOT HAPPEN," Chandrasekhar said, adding that he too had "just realised" about these "students."His remarks came amid an online debate after photographs and old social media posts of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Das's reported meeting with Khalid resurfaced following the recent student protests at Jantar Mantar over NEET-UG examination irregularities.(With inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Kerala BJP president Rajeev Chandrasekhar took a swipe at leaders of the recent student protests in Delhi. He cited an old social media post by CJP leader Saurav Das praising jailed student activist Umar Khalid. In the post, Das had described Khalid as the "bravest" and said he had "mad respect" for him.

Article Title: CJP protest in Mumbai: Cop ‘inappropriately touches’ woman in video, stirs row
Article Text:
The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.





MUMBAI: A viral video from the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Thursday, showing a policeman allegedly inappropriately touching a woman protester, stirred up a fresh controversy on Friday, with the opposition demanding his dismissal.The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.DCP (operations) Akbar Pathan said, “The official was trying to hold on to a male protester and a lady stepped in while he was looking away. Senior officers have verified all the facts and minutely assessed the video to ascertain the facts,” he said.Another police official said, “Since the video went viral late Thursday night, our senior cyber crime experts carefully zoomed in on the footage, verified it, and found that there was no misconduct.”The controversy came a day after another viral video showed a police constable, who was working as a driver, allegedly threatening young protesters that drugs would be planted on them and their career would be ruined if they continued participating in protests.The latest video quickly went viral on social media, with several opposition politicians demanding action against the policeman. Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded an apology from CM Devendra Fadnavis and dismissal of the policeman.In a post on X, Sapkal said, “The one who calls himself Devabhaau has turned out to be Duryodhan! Devabhaau’s police have become so rogue that they are violating the modesty of female students the age of their own daughters.”Mumbai Congress president and MP Varsha Gaikwad said, “What happened to a girl during the protest in Mumbai is deeply painful and disturbing. It is wrong to speak of the ‘Ladki Bahin’ scheme while treating young women in such a manner. It is a matter of shame that women are allegedly being mistreated in the land of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. False cases are being registered against students, and they are being threatened. ”Congress has organised statewide candlelight marches and ‘satyagraha’ in Maharashtra on Saturday to express solidarity with the protesting students.
Article Summary: The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage. The controversy came a day after another viral video showed a police constable, who was working as a driver, allegedly threatening young protesters.

Article Title: 3 years on, SIT probe complete in just 10% of Manipur riot cases
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.
Article Summary: Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives. Only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by state police. CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.

Article Title: 'Ab aayega aur maza!' CJP says 'time is ticking' as farmers announce march to Jantar Mantar on Sunday
Article Text:
CJP's Saurav Das alleges tanks being transported to Delhi
