Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the call for a tough stance if demands are not met? Strongly agree Disagree 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das on Saturday urged the Centre to accept the protesters' demands, alleging that the government was transporting tanks to Delhi while the student agitation continued."Ab aayega aur maza! The government must understand that it can either bomb the peaceful protesters using the tanks it is transporting to Delhi (I mean, what are they trying to do by transporting these? Kill their own children? Is this where we have come in Gandhi's India?) Or, accept demands. The time is ticking!" Das said in a post on X.He made the remarks while sharing a post by the Bharatiya Kisan Union announcing that it would join the ongoing student protest at Jantar Mantar.The development comes as CJP reiterated that it may adopt a "tough stance" if the Centre does not clarify its position on the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Speaking to reporters, CJP activist Ashutosh Ranka said the meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh was constructive, but added that the organisation was still awaiting the government's response to its primary demand."Yesterday's meeting yielded a positive response regarding compensation and legal matters, reaching an in-principle agreement. We hope to receive that written agreement today. However, no concrete decision has been made regarding our main demand. Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.""Mainstream media reports suggest sources are saying Pradhan will not step down. If he does not resign, the government should state it clearly, as there is no point in continuing these meetings. We will then decide on our next steps. If the government continues this approach, we will be forced to take a tough stance," Ranka said.Earlier, activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh after the Union government gave a written assurance on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said strict action would be taken against those responsible for the alleged paper leaks. He also said the Union Cabinet would consider a draft Bill proposing fast-track courts and stricter punishment for offenders.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das urged the Centre to accept the protesters' demands. He alleges that the government was transporting tanks to Delhi while the student agitation continued. The development comes as CJP reiterated that it may adopt a "tough stance" if the Centre does not clarify its position on the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Article Title: US restores $600 million for Gavi vaccine alliance, keeps WHO cut off
Article Text:
During his first term in 2020, Trump temporarily suspended US funding to the organisation.

The United States has approved the release of $600 million in funding for Gavi, the global vaccine alliance, but has decided that none of the money will be routed through the World Health Organization (WHO), dealing another financial setback to the UN health agency.In a joint statement, the US Department of State and the Department of Health and Human Services said the US government would not provide funding to the WHO through Gavi.The decision follows directions issued by President Donald Trump, who asked Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and secretary of state Marco Rubio to negotiate reforms with Gavi before any long-term US support is restored.Republican Senator Susan Collins, who had urged the administration to resume funding for the international immunisation programme, welcomed the move.According to the State Department, Gavi has agreed to work with its governing board and partner countries to gradually replace vaccines containing mercury with mercury-free alternatives. The latest decision continues Trump's long-running dispute with the WHO.During his first term in 2020, Trump temporarily suspended US funding to the organisation, accusing it of mishandling the Covid-19 pandemic and amplifying what he called China's "disinformation" about the virus.He argued that the WHO's actions contributed to the wider spread of the outbreak.At the time, the United States was the WHO's largest financial contributor, providing more than $400 million in 2019, which accounted for about 15 per cent of the organisation's budget.On the first day of his second term on January 20, 2025, Trump announced that the US would withdraw from the WHO and halted American financial contributions to the agency.Health experts have said the administration's decisions appear to be driven more by ideological considerations than by strategic public health priorities.The WHO receives funding through mandatory contributions from member states as well as voluntary donations from governments and other partners.With an annual budget of about $3.4 billion, the WHO operates on significantly fewer resources than the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, which received $9.3 billion in core funding in 2023.The organisation uses its funding to support vaccination campaigns and programmes to prevent and treat diseases such as polio, tuberculosis, HIV, malaria and measles, particularly in countries with limited healthcare systems.It also coordinates emergency health responses in conflict-affected regions, including Gaza, Sudan and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, among others.
Article Summary: The United States has approved the release of $600 million in funding for Gavi, the global vaccine alliance. But it has decided that none of the money will be routed through the World Health Organization (WHO) The decision follows directions issued by President Donald Trump. During his first term in 2020, Trump temporarily suspended US funding to the organisation.

Article Title: Ousted PM Sheikh Hasina plans Bangladesh return: 'I may be killed, I may be sent to prison'
Article Text: Bangladesh's ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday said she was determined to return to her country by December despite facing the possibility of arrest, imprisonment or even execution.The 78-year-old former leader, who has been living in New Delhi since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024, said she was prepared to face the consequences of returning home."I may be killed. I may be arrested. I may be sent to prison," Hasina said in an email response to questions by AFP."I am fully aware of my fate. Still, I want to go back because my people are calling me," she added.Earlier this month, Hasina had also told Reuters that she and her political allies would return from exile and face the courts in Bangladesh."My party leaders and workers are being subjected to tremendous repression," she had told Reuters. "If death comes, I want it to come on my own soil, where my parents are buried and where their blood was shed," she added.Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal over her government's handling of the 2024 student-led protests that ultimately ended her 15-year rule.The protests began as demonstrations against the country's government job quota system but quickly evolved into a nationwide anti-government movement after security forces launched a crackdown on protesters.Thousands were injured, while many were detained during the months-long protests.As the demonstrations intensified and spread across the country, Hasina resigned and fled in August 2024, ending her tenure as prime minister.Following the change in government, Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal initiated multiple cases against Hasina and several of her former ministers over allegations of crimes against humanity linked to the crackdown.Her Awami League has since been banned from political activities, while several senior party leaders have been arrested or are facing legal proceedings.Earlier this year, Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) chief Tarique Rahman was sworn in as the country's new prime minister. He became the first elected male premier after decades of politics dominated by Sheikh Hasina and his mother, former prime minister Khaleda Zia, a long-running rivalry often described as the "battle of the begums."
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has been living in New Delhi since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024. She was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal over her government's handling of the 2024 student-led protests. The protests began as demonstrations against the country's government job quota system.

Article Title: Inside US-Saudi nuclear deal: Trump opens critical door in Middle East; why Pakistan is biggest loser
Article Text:
The nuclear map of the Middle East and South Asia is set to be redrawn.

The US-Saudi nuclear pact

The new 30‑year US-Saudi deal authorises American companies to help Riyadh build reactors, transfer advanced tech and cooperate on the fuel cycle.

The Saudi arrangement loosens long‑standing US non‑proliferation guardrails.

Atoms & alignment

The Israel rider

Trump has said the Saudi nuclear pact hinges on the kingdom joining the Abraham Accords.

Managing the inevitable

Pakistan left out in the cold

Countries with nuclear stockpiles.

A future nuclear triangle

A critical point

The nuclear map of the Middle East and South Asia is set to be redrawn after the US signed a historic 30-year civilian nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia , opening a potential pathway for domestic uranium enrichment on Saudi soil under American technical oversight.It is a move driven as much by US president Donald Trump's worldview and domestic politics as by the administration’s long-term design to lock Saudi Arabia into an American-led security architecture while keeping China and Russia out of the kingdom’s atomic future.While Washington frames the move as a triumph of commercial strategy and security integration, the broader regional fallout paints a starkly different picture.Above all, Pakistan emerges as the ultimate strategic loser.For decades, Islamabad enjoyed a unique position of leverage as the custodian of the Islamic world’s only operational atomic arsenal. The US-Saudi pact fundamentally dismantles that monopoly, marginalises Pakistan's leverage over Riyadh, and accelerates a tri-polar nuclear reality across West Asia featuring Israel, Iran, and Saudi Arabia.The new 30‑year US-Saudi civil nuclear cooperation agreement authorises American companies to help Riyadh build reactors, transfer advanced nuclear technology and cooperate on the fuel cycle, including potentially sensitive stages such as uranium enrichment.Unlike the so‑called "gold standard" deal with the UAE, which explicitly forswore enrichment and reprocessing, the Saudi arrangement loosens long‑standing US non‑proliferation guardrails , opening the door to domestic enrichment on Saudi soil after a defined period. Arms control experts note that under the agreed framework, Washington and Riyadh will conduct a study on the commercial viability of enrichment in the kingdom; if justified, the US would build a so‑called “black box” enrichment facility in Saudi Arabia and retain nominal control of the technology.But even conservative analyses concede that after about 10 years, Saudi Arabia would be free to develop indigenous enrichment capabilities or turn to alternative suppliers if it chose to move beyond civilian use, creating a latent weapons option.Like all signatories to the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, Saudi Arabia has already committed to not developing an atomic bomb and consented to international inspections. But Washington has traditionally sought extra protections.Almost all of the 26 nuclear cooperation agreements the US has inked so far included what’s known as an “additional protocol” signed with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). This means the IAEA can thoroughly inspect all nuclear facilities.However, its latest pact with Saudi Arabia does not include an “additional protocol” of extra international oversight.For the Trump administration, the deal is a convergence of ideology, grand strategy and industrial policy.At one level, it reflects Trump's transactional approach: major nuclear contracts for US firms, billions in potential reactor and fuel deals, and a promise to "bring back" America’s nuclear industry in the face of competition from China, Russia, France and South Korea.At a deeper level, the agreement is a tool to anchor Saudi Arabia irreversibly in a US‑centric orbit, at a time when Riyadh has flirted with Chinese and Russian nuclear offers and diversified its security partnerships.By tying Saudi Arabia's most sensitive technology to American hardware, standards and oversight, Trump is betting that the kingdom’s energy transition, defence modernisation and even future deterrent posture will remain structurally dependent on Washington, not Beijing or Moscow.Should the pact fail, even at this late stage, countries with established nuclear industries have expressed interest or are seen as potential partners for Saudi Arabia’s nuclear programme.State-owned China National Nuclear Corp (CNNC) reportedly submitted a bid in 2023 to construct a nuclear plant.Russia's state nuclear firm Rosatom, which built a nuclear plant in Egypt, has also signed preliminary cooperation agreements with Riyadh. Other potential contenders include South Korea, which built reactors in the neighbouring United Arab Emirates, and France.The choice of partner will likely depend on technological offerings, financing, and geopolitical alignment, including conditions related to nuclear fuel handling.A distinctive feature of Trump's nuclear diplomacy is the embedding of the Saudi deal within a broader vision of "mandatory Abraham Accords" – in effect, requiring Riyadh's normalisation with Israel as the political price of accessing the nuclear package.Reporting from US and Israeli outlets indicates that Trump has pushed to make Saudi participation in an expanded Abraham framework a condition for full implementation of the nuclear agreement. In this logic, nuclear cooperation is leverage: the carrot that nudges Saudi Arabia into a formal strategic alignment with Israel against Iran, while delivering Trump a signature diplomatic trophy he can sell to his domestic base and donors.It also allows the administration to present the nuclear deal not as an isolated proliferation risk but as part of a grand bargain – peace with Israel and a stronger anti‑Iran coalition under American leadership. Saudi Arabia has so far not responded to the claim.However, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said that if Riyadh does not join the Abraham Accords "the deal is off".Trump's advisors have long argued that Saudi Arabia’s nuclear ambitions are a given, not a variable.Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has publicly stated that if Iran gets a bomb, Saudi Arabia will quickly follow, signalling that the kingdom views a nuclear hedge as a necessary insurance policy in a deteriorating security environment.In that context, the administration's internal justification is that it is better to channel Saudi nuclear development through a US‑supervised framework than to push Riyadh into the arms of Chinese or Russian suppliers, who would likely impose weaker safeguards.In other words, Washington is not trying to prevent Saudi Arabia from ever acquiring a latent nuclear option; it is trying to ensure that, if and when such an option matures, it emerges within a system where the US has maximum visibility, contractual leverage and political influence.Until now Pakistan has had the rare distinction of being the only nuclear-armed Islamic state. That status bolstered its self-image as a protector of the Muslim world, reinforced by decades of defence ties with Saudi Arabia.For years analysts feared Riyadh might one day lean on Pakistan for a deterrent: weapons, technology, or a tacit shield. A 2025 mutual-defence pact, whose language hinted Pakistani nuclear assets could aid Saudi Arabia in extremis, seemed to confirm that risk.The US-Saudi nuclear framework changes the calculus. First, it expects Saudi nuclear activity to be placed under IAEA safeguards tied to US-origin technology, which makes any covert Pakistani role far riskier and politically costly for Riyadh. Second, as Saudi Arabia deepens ties with India and embraces US-led economic corridors like the India-Middle East-Europe route, a tight Saudi-Pakistan axis looks less likely.For Pakistan, the consequences are both symbolic and practical. The bomb has long been a source of pride, parity with India, and a claim to leadership in the Islamic ummah. If Saudi Arabia develops its own nuclear infrastructure, Pakistan’s claim to be the sole Muslim nuclear power will become time-bound and hollow. Gulf states gaining independent nuclear paths reduce Islamabad’s ability to monetise or politicise its nuclear expertise.Over time Pakistan risks being seen not as the indispensable Muslim nuclear state but as one among several — and arguably the weakest economically, with the heaviest proliferation baggage from the AQ Khan era.Pakistan’s complicated ties with Washington and Beijing also limit its ability to act as a nuclear supplier or trainer for Riyadh.Symbolically, the US-Saudi deal completes a shift that began when Gulf monarchies warmed to India and Israel: they now prioritise economics and technology and prefer partnerships with Washington, New Delhi and Tel Aviv over outsourcing deterrence to Pakistan. If, within a decade, Saudi Arabia runs advanced enrichment and reactor infrastructure based on US technology, the centre of gravity for “Islamic nuclear power” will have moved from South Asia to the Arabian Peninsula.Looking out over the next decade, the logic of the Trump-Saudi arrangement points towards a West Asia where three key states: Israel, Iran and Saudi Arabia – either possess or are a short sprint away from nuclear weapons.Israel is already widely believed to maintain an undeclared but operational nuclear arsenal , under a longstanding policy of opacity.Iran, despite dithering on nuclear agreements, has substantially advanced its enrichment capabilities and possesses a short “breakout” timeline to a bomb if it chooses.Saudi Arabia, under the new deal, acquires the legal, technical and industrial scaffolding of a civil programme that can, over time, be repurposed into a weapons‑relevant capability, especially if Iran crosses the nuclear weapons threshold.The 10‑year horizon embedded in the agreement – after which Riyadh faces fewer constraints on seeking alternative enrichment partners – is precisely the sort of timeline in which a latent nuclear option could mature into a credible deterrent.This triangular nuclear geometry would mark a historic departure from the era when Israel alone held a nuclear monopoly in the region.It also risks a cascade effect, with other regional players – Turkey, Egypt, even the UAE – reassessing whether they can remain non‑nuclear. Critically, this approach shifts US non‑proliferation policy from prevention to hierarchy.Instead of insisting that no new state in West Asia should get enrichment or weapons‑relevant technology, Washington is implicitly endorsing a tiered order: friendly states may have latent capabilities within a regulated framework; adversaries like Iran must be constrained; and global rivals like China and Russia are to be excluded from building those capabilities.This is a radical break from the “gold standard” approach and explains why arms control advocates accuse the deal of "compromising essential non‑proliferation guardrails".If the trajectory outlined in the US-Saudi deal holds, West Asia in the mid‑2030s could feature three central nuclear players: Israel with its established but undeclared arsenal; Iran with a short or accomplished breakout capability; and Saudi Arabia with a US‑incubated nuclear infrastructure capable of swift militarisation in a crisis.Around this triangle, American forces and bases would operate as both deterrent and guarantor, even as China and Russia seek entry points through alternative energy and defence deals. In that triangle, Pakistan is conspicuous not by its presence but by its relative absence.Once the only Islamic state with the bomb, it risks becoming a peripheral nuclear power in a region whose atomic future is being rewritten by Washington and Riyadh – a future in which the most consequential Islamic nuclear story may not be the one Pakistan told about itself in 1998, but the one Saudi Arabia writes under American supervision a decade from now.
Article Summary: The nuclear map of the Middle East and South Asia is set to be redrawn. The US signed a historic 30-year civilian nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia. It opens a potential pathway for domestic uranium enrichment on Saudi soil under American technical oversight. Pakistan emerges as the ultimate strategic loser.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.

Article Title: Delhi Mosque Demolition: Delhi Demolition Drive Near Faiz-e-Elahi Mosque: Police Clash During MCD Action
Article Text:
Delhi demolition drive: MCD carries out action near Faiz-e-Elahi mosque following HC order; 5 cops injured in stone pelting

Delhi: 5 Cops Injured, 10 Detained As Anti-Encroachment Drive Near Mosque Turns Violent

Demolition drive at Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque near Turkman Gate in Delhi on Wednesday. Image Credit: Tarun Rawat/TNN







NEW DELHI: Multiple police personnel were injured during a demolition drive in central Delhi early on Wednesday after locals and miscreants attacked them with stones.The police is trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting and will initiate strict action against them.Delhi Police have registered an FIR against unknown persons and around 10 people have been detained for questioning so far, officials said.Police are scanning CCTV footage, ground visuals and body-camera recordings to identify those involved in the attack on the police team.While the FIR has been lodged against unidentified persons, investigators said four to five suspects have already been identified and further legal action will follow.Special commissioner (Law and Order) Ravindra Yadav said that the action started around 1 am."MCD conducted demolition as per the high court's orders on the encroached land. Stones were pelted at the police at night. We used minimal force to push back."DCP (Central) Nidhin Valsan said, "The action is still ongoing. We deployed our staff for security. 4 to 5 officers suffered minor injuries. As soon as we get the CCTV camera footage, ground footage, and body camera footage, we will identify the miscreants and take legal action."The demolition was carried out by the MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area. The drive kicked off around 1 am, with around 17 bulldozers pressed into service.The action followed an order of the Delhi High Court, which declared a dispensary and a community hall adjoining the mosque illegal and directed their removal.The administration appealed to local residents to maintain peace.Anticipating major disruptions, the Delhi Traffic Police also issued a traffic advisory, warning of congestion on several key roads on Wednesday. Traffic around Ramlila Maidan and adjoining areas is expected to remain affected through the day.
Article Summary: 5 cops injured in stone pelting during demolition drive in central Delhi. Police are trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting. The demolition was carried out by MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area.

Article Title: Laxmi Nagar assault: New clip shows SUV crashing into house; accused Omkar Yadav claims self-defence in viral video
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Another CCTV clip related to the Laxmi Nagar assault has surfaced, showing a group of men arriving first, opening a gate and assaulting a man. Moments later, a Thar SUV was seen speeding towards the house and crashing into the wall, after which several men got out of it and the assault continued. Meanwhile, accused Omkar Yadav has released a video on social media defending his brother, gym caretaker and key accused Satish Yadav alias Pintu Yadav.A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault recently when the man was beaten up, his wife was said to be molested, and their son was stripped and assaulted on the street.The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business, leading to the dispute. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage-related issue, Yadav, along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son, a senior officer said.An earlier CCTV footage had shown the couple's son being dragged onto the road, stripped and beaten up by a group of four-five men. The presence of police personnel in parts of the footage also raised questions. Police claimed the assault stopped after they arrived while the victims alleged that they were beaten up in full view of the cops, a claim that is being verified.According to the complaint, the couple's son came out after hearing the commotion and was assaulted. The couple also said their two sons had left the house following the attack.Police said main accused Yadav was arrested while the other accused were absconding. Omkar, one of the absconding accused, posted a video on social media, saying his brother had been working with the complainant for "20-25 years" and was running the gym for the past "12-13 years". He questioned why objections over the gym were raised only in the past five-six months. "If we captured the land, why did she start complaining only now?" he asked.Omkar further alleged that the legal proceedings were "one-sided" and claimed that he was also being targeted. He identified himself as a worker of a party and alleged that he was being defamed by an opposition party.Referring to the incident, Omkar said, "On Jan 2, I got a call from my brother. I reached the spot after 10-15 minutes. If I am seen kicking two or three times in the video, it was in self-defence. They started hitting first."A case has been registered at the Laxmi Nagar police station under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint, criminal trespass, assault or use of criminal force to outrage the modesty of a woman, acts intended to insult a woman's modesty and criminal intimidation.
Article Summary: A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault. The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage- related issue, Yadav along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son.

Article Title: 'Answer now': CJP's Saurav Das cites Rahul Gandhi's claims, targets Amit Shah over July 20 police action
Article Text:
CJP spokesperson Saurav Das on Wednesday demanded 'answers' from Amit Shah , citing allegations made by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in the Lok Sabha.

CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das shared on 'X'

(With inputs from PTI)





NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) on Wednesday demanded 'answers' from Union home minister Amit Shah over the July 20 police action against student protesters, citing allegations made by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in the Lok Sabha.CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das shared on 'X' and wrote, "This raises serious concerns about the Home Minister's role in July 20 Police Brutality case. He must be held accountable. Every life is precious. A student lost his vision for life at the Home Minister's order! Answer now."The remarks came after Rahul , speaking during the Lok Sabha debate on the anti-paper leak bill, alleged that Shah was responsible for the police action against students protesting over the alleged NEET paper leak."The home minister put the pellets into the blood of our students; he ordered the students of India to be shot," Rahul claimed in the House. He also alleged that only the home minister or the Prime Minister "can authorise" such use of force.Rahul further questioned Shah's absence from the debate, saying he had seen the home minister sitting in his car but that "he is not present in the Lok Sabha because he is scared."Many of Rahul's remarks in the Lok Sabha were later expunged by the Speaker.However, outside Parliament and later at a press conference, the Congress leader repeated the allegations and demanded Shah's removal."There can be just two options - the Home Minister gave the order for firing (at protesters), the other is that the Home Minister did not know that there will be firing," Rahul told reporters."In the first case, he is culpable. In the second case, he is incompetent, there can be no other option," he said.At a press conference, Rahul alleged that Shah either "ordered that students be shot with pellet guns and beaten with lathis having nails" or was unaware of the action. "If he ordered it, he is culpable and if he did not know then he is incompetent," he said, adding that pellet guns could not be used without the home minister's permission.Claiming Shah was "guilty," Rahul urged the government to remove him from office."Our advice to the government is to sack Amit Shah and order an independent high-powered committee monitored by the Supreme Court" to investigate the matter, he said."Shah must go, he has shot our students and he must be held accountable," Rahul alleged.The BJP rejected the allegations, accusing Rahul of making false claims.Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said Rahul was attempting to mislead the House by claiming Shah had ordered police firing during the protests.BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra also denied the allegations."Rahul Rahul said that bullets were fired at the students. He lied. No bullet was fired. He also lied that Home Minister Amit Shah ordered the firing," Patra said.The exchange comes amid continued political sparring over the July 20 CJP-led protest march to Parliament and the police action against demonstrators.
Article Summary: CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das shared on 'X' and wrote, "This raises serious concerns about the Home Minister's role in July 20 Police Brutality case. He must be held accountable. Every life is precious. A student lost his vision for life at the home Minister's order! Answer now"

Article Title: Left-backed student groups stage fresh protest at Jantar Mantar
Article Text:
(PTI Photo Used For Only Representational Purpose): Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) supporters raise slogans during a protest at the Jantar Mantar.





NEW DELHI: Students from several Left-affiliated organisations held a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Wednesday, demanding the release of students detained during recent demonstrations and calling for an end to what they described as the "criminalisation" of student protests.The demonstration, held under the banner "Student-Youth Unity; Long Live", came days after a month-long agitation that ended with the resignation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.The protest followed a joint call by Left organisations, including the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union (JNUSU), to mobilise "against the police crackdown on the students and youth of Bihar, Bengal and other states".Members of several student groups, including the All India Students' Association (AISA), Students' Federation of India (SFI), All India Students' Federation (AISF), Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS), All India Democratic Students' Organisation (AIDSO), DSF, PDSU, PSA, PSYA, ACNS, COLLECTIVE, DISHA and PACHHAS, joined the demonstration.Protesters raised slogans including "Chhatron ki giraftaari band karo" (stop arresting students) and "Chhatron ka criminalisation nahi chalega" (stop the criminalisation of students).Speaking at the protest, a DISHA activist appealed to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which had led the earlier agitation, to call for another mobilisation at Jantar Mantar."If the CJP gives a call even today, students will return to Jantar Mantar. The movement can still be revived. If no fresh call is given, students will lose faith, and that would amount to a defeat of this movement," she said.Several demonstrators carried placards demanding action against police personnel involved in the use of force during the July 20 protest march. One placard read: "Punish the policemen responsible for the brutality on 20th July".Addressing the gathering, student leaders alleged that participants in the recent protests were being targeted by the authorities and claimed that several social media accounts linked to the movement had been blocked."We can see how the authorities are targeting students across the country for protesting. We want to tell you that you are not alone; we stand with you. If they think students are scared of lathi-charge, they are wrong," a member of the Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS) said.An AISA member alleged that more than 300 students had been arrested in Bihar in connection with the protests and claimed that several detainees were injured during police action.Referring to an incident in Bihar, she alleged that four students sustained bullet injuries after alleged firing with AK-47 rifles near AIIMS, Patna, and were admitted to a hospital in the city."Two students suffered life-altering injuries. One has undergone surgery and another still requires a second surgery. One of them is unable to move his shoulder," she alleged.The protesters demanded the immediate release of all students detained in connection with the recent demonstrations and called for an end to police action against student activists.
Article Summary: Demonstration came days after a month-long agitation that ended with the resignation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The protest followed a joint call by Left organisations to mobilise "against the police crackdown on the students and youth of Bihar, Bengal and other states"

Article Title: Awareness session helps 10-year-old girl break silence on 3-year-long molestation, two van drivers arrested
Article Text: New Delhi: Two school van drivers have been arrested for allegedly molesting a 10-year-old girl repeatedly over three years in north Delhi’s Civil Lines, police said Wednesday. The survivor, a Class VI student, confided in a teacher following a classroom awareness session on ’good touch and bad touch’.According to police, both men were employed as drivers for the private van that transported the girl to and from her school in Civil Lines. She was subjected to inappropriate physical touching inside the van since she was seven years old, police said.The alleged long-running abuse occurred at various points during her daily commute, with the most recent incident taking place on July 21 near Khyber Pass in Civil Lines. Out of fear and intimidation, she kept quiet for three years, police said.A senior officer said, “The school recently organised a routine body safety awareness session. Prompted by the lesson on distinguishing between safe and unsafe touch, the girl approached her class teacher and recounted the repeated misconduct by the two drivers.”The teacher immediately alerted the girl’s parents, who accompanied their daughter to the local police post to lodge a complaint.“A case was registered under sections 8 and 10 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, which pertain to the punishment for sexual assault and aggravated sexual assault on a child,” the officer said.Following preliminary inquiries and verification of the allegations, police arrested both accused. Investigators are questioning them and verifying whether other children who used the same service were also subjected to similar behaviour.In a similar incident, a three-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted by a caretaker inside a school in west Delhi’s Janakpuri in May.
Article Summary: Two school van drivers have been arrested for allegedly molesting a 10-year-old girl repeatedly over three years in north Delhi’s Civil Lines. The alleged long- running abuse occurred at various points during her daily commute, with the most recent incident taking place on July 21.

Article Title: No vada pav near Mumbai schools? FDA bans junk food sales within 50 metres
Article Text:
Students can be seen enjoying vada pav after school. (AI-generated image used for representational purpose)





MUMBAI: Vada pav, samosas, cold drinks, chocolates and ice creams will no longer be allowed to be sold, distributed or advertised inside schools or within a 50-metre radius of school premises in Maharashtra under a new statewide order issued by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).FDA commissioner Tukaram Munde said school authorities will be held accountable for implementing the ban and warned of action against principals and school managements that fail to comply."I want to make it clear that excess fat, excess trans fat and excess sugar products, including deeply fried foods, excessive sugar drinks, vada pav, samosa, cold drinks, chocolates and ice cream, such junk foods are strictly not allowed inside schools to be sold, not be distributed freely, advertise and also not in the surrounding (50 metres range). Principal and school management should implement this strictly, and there should also be awareness about it among parents," he said.The official said action will be taken against the principal and the school management who don't comply and follow."We will start inspections across the state soon. FDA along with school management will be happy to take a workshop at district level and taluka level to implement it smoothly," Munde added.He also spoke about complaints related to the alleged MPSC paper leak."We received an email from an individual on the 21st. We recorded the person's statement on the 24th. MPSC is an independent body, and it conducts the Food and Drug Inspector examination. We have forwarded the statement and all the documents we received to the MPSC," Tukaram Munde said.In a separate incident earlier this month, the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the food licences of three eateries in Mumbai after inspections allegedly found serious violations of hygiene and food safety norms.According to the FDA, six inspections were carried out, following which the licences of three food businesses in Bhendi Bazaar and Umarkhadi were suspended for failing to comply with food safety regulations.The FDA said one establishment's food licence was suspended on July 14 after a re-inspection conducted on July 13 found that 25 major deficiencies identified earlier had not been rectified. The outlet had first been inspected on April 16, following which an improvement notice was issued on April 28.During the re-inspection, officials found wet and slippery kitchen floors, absence of records for raw material procurement, no testing records for drinking water quality, lack of documentation regarding the quality of cooking oil, failure to maintain proper segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, and open windows without insect-proof screens, allowing pest entry.(With inputs from ANI)
Article Summary: Vada pav, samosas, chocolates and ice creams will no longer be allowed to be sold, distributed or advertised inside schools or within a 50-metre radius of school premises. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner Tukaram Munde said school authorities will be held accountable for implementing the ban.

Article Title: Mumbai police arrest science graduate from West Bengal for creating, selling APK files to scammers
Article Text: Mumbai: The D B Marg police arrested a 26-year-old science graduate, S K Mandal, from West Bengal for allegedly preparing and selling APK files to fraudsters who used them to cheat gullible victims.“We have arrested Mandal from West Bengal. He is originally from Jharkhand. The Android Application Package (APK) files prepared by the accused were involved in crimes in the city and there are 512 complaints on helpline number 1930/ NCCRP against these files. Mandal used to sell APK files for Rs 15,000 each. We are examining his laptop and mobile phone,” said zonal DCP Ragasudha R.Mandal was arrested by the police which were probing a cyber cheating case of Rs 70,500 where the complainant was duped after she clicked a fake Mahanagar Gas Ltd APK file.Mandal allegedly sold 91 files to various cyber cheat gangs.There are 2,993 complaints registered against these APK files on the national cybercrime reporting portal (NCCRP). In these cases, around Rs 63.7 crore was siphoned off from victims’ accounts.Ragasudha said, “We have seized 10 mobile phones, one laptop, seven SIM cards, four credit/debit cards, 967 APK files and found the database of banking information of 37,200 individuals from the accused.During the probe, we found that 91 APK files created by the arrested accused were sold to other accused. Through these sold APK files, a total of 2,993 (including 512 in Maharashtra especially Mumbai), the general public were cheated of Rs 63.69 crore. ” Police said that had the accused sold all his files, the fraudsters could have cheated the public of hundreds of crores.Police said Mandal would sell the APK files through a social media channel. The buyers would contact him and he would develop and send the APK files as per their demand and receive money mostly in cash.The fraudsters, who contact a victim, generally send an APK file with different names of companies or institutions. They ask to update the electricity bill, gas connection and RTO challan, and threaten disconnection or action if not done. They send an APK file to the victim through WhatsApp . Once a victim opens an APK file and keys in some details, the fraudsters take control of their mobile phone and siphon off money from their account.

Article Title: Citing job risks, Maha govt offers pay perk to drugs task force
Article Text:
Officers and personnel from the task force will be given a 30% incentive allowance

Mumbai:





The state govt has announced a 30% incentive allowance for police officers and personnel serving in Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF), citing the hazardous nature of their work and the risks involved in tackling organised drug networks.The state has also created 346 posts for ANTF, which draws officers and personnel from the state police force.According to a govt resolution (GR) issued on Wednesday, the incentive will come into effect on Aug 1 and will be equivalent to 30% of the basic pay under the Seventh Pay Commission . Govt has made a budgetary provision of Rs 5.9 crore for the allowance. It said the incentive is aimed at attracting capable and efficient personnel to the specialised unit and strengthening its ability to take stringent preventive and enforcement action against narcotics trafficking.The incentive, however, will cease once an officer or personnel is repatriated to their parent cadre from ANTF.ANTF carries out intelligence operations, raids and investigations against narcotics trafficking and international and organised criminal gangs. It is also empowered to coordinate with central agencies and investigate cases involving pan-Maharashtra and interstate drug trafficking networks.Govt said those working in the unit frequently risk their lives during intelligence gathering, raids and investigations. Their handling of hazardous narcotic substances also exposes them to the risk of serious physical and mental injury.Through the incentive, govt hopes to induct more talent. “Nowadays, officers are not willing to work in these cells as the timings are very irregular. The work requires round-the-clock surveillance,” said an officer. Officials also pointed to limited funds for intelligence gathering.The demanding nature of narcotics investigations has also contributed to burnout among personnel, officers said. Continuous exposure to hardened criminals, high-pressure operations and prolonged periods of vigilance can affect morale and personal well-being, they said.Legal scrutiny is another major concern for investigators. Cases under stringent provisions of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act require strict adherence to procedures, as even minor lapses can have serious departmental or judicial consequences. “If a case falls flat in court, there are chances that we will be pulled up by senior officers, sometimes without any fault on our part,” said a DCP who has worked in the anti-narcotics cell.Officers said high-profile seizures and sensitive investigations also attract scrutiny from internal authorities and external anti-corruption agencies. Personnel are required to maintain detailed records and ensure the safe custody of seized narcotic substances. Any allegation of loss, tampering, substitution or mishandling of seized material can result in serious questions being raised against the officers concerned.
Article Summary: The state has also created 346 posts for ANTF, which draws officers and personnel from the state police force. The incentive will come into effect on Aug 1 and will be equivalent to 30% of the basic pay under the Seventh Pay Commission. Govt has made a budgetary provision of Rs 5.9 crore for the allowance.
